evidence.notes: Vendor settings expose browser integration and MCP customizations. The gemini lock records only bash:safe, read and write; it is a registry declaration, not a native tool inventory. Antigravity has no standalone adapter here. No historical native tool list, web setting or extension inventory is recorded.

Vendor settings distinguish review and unattended authority. The local gemini class maps to Antigravity, but the fleet launcher and its effective permissions are not in this checkout. No historical permission or container settings are recorded; the four-harness standalone container cannot establish Antigravity containment.

The 55 records contain imported model labels (google/gemini-3.1-pro: 55). The importer maps labels to provider ids, not native execution telemetry. No per-run native model event or resolved-model proof is committed, so CCMODEL-01 cannot be verified; no model mismatch is inferred.

All 55 rows record high, derived from the imported model-label mapping. Vendor effort is model-dependent and selectable; native resolved effort and the historical CLI version are absent. Other compared harness rows have null effort, so equivalence across comparisons is not established.

The current shared staging function constructs one task prompt plus the same workspace guard without a harness branch. Antigravity has no standalone argv here; its historical launcher is external. Imported bundles contain neither the delivered prompt/hash nor effective system, project or persona instructions; historical prompt parity is not verifiable.

Current standalone defaults are 3600 seconds, 2 CPUs, 2048 MiB and 256 processes, shared by its four adapters; no per-harness turn or token cap is supplied in their argv. These are benchmark limits, not vendor defaults. Historical fleet descriptors omit timeout, CPU, memory and turn/token limits, and wall_seconds is null. Battery admission budgets do not establish per-run resource parity.

The repository parses native harness events, but imported bundles retain verdict summaries without tool-call records or completeness evidence. Standalone output overflow is rejected before grading, which does not establish historical fleet capture. Whole-record OCEXPORT-01 compliance cannot be verified from these results.

The only imported descriptor labels transport as vendor. The external launcher and effective endpoint/route are not recorded, so the absence of a proxy or gateway cannot be verified. No private endpoint is needed for this audit; a sanitized route and rewrite description would suffice.

All 55 records have harness.version=null. Each record does have a config_hash with a matching descriptor, but the CLI version requirement fails. A descriptor hash does not recover the missing native version or the omitted settings.

checklist.check: The harness exposes its vendor-default tool set: no tool removed, none added, and native web access left at the vendor default and recorded.
The harness runs in its vendor's non-interactive mode with equivalent authority; the sandbox boundary is the container, the same for every harness.
The model the harness actually ran, read from its own telemetry, is the one recorded (CCMODEL-01).
The reasoning or effort level is recorded, and is the vendor default or the same named level across compared rows.
Every harness gets the same task prompt and no harness-specific instructions beyond its vendor default system prompt.
Wall-clock timeout, container CPU and memory, and turn or token limits are the same for every harness, or the vendor default and recorded.
The harness's tool-call record is captured whole, never truncated, so a read-evidence check cannot fail on capture (OCEXPORT-01).
When a model is reached through a proxy or gateway, any request rewriting it does is part of the recorded configuration (KIMIEMPTY-01).
Harness CLI version and configuration hash are recorded with every result.
